 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The ATP Finals are officially underway, with Alexander Zverev and Ben Shelton getting off to winning starts in the John McEnroe group. 
 In the opening match of the year-end showpiece, world number one Zverev defeated debutant Rafael Jodar fairly comfortably, overcoming the 20-year-old Spaniard in straight sets, 6-4, 6-4, without conceding a break of serve.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Ben Shelton then took centre stage in Turin with his new coach, Juan Carlos Ferrero, watching on and clinched a maiden ATP Finals win over Arthur Fils, 6-2, 3-6, 6-3.
 Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images
 Greg Rusedski predicts who will win the 2026 ATP Finals in Turin
 There is still plenty of tennis left to play in the round-robin phase of the ATP Finals, but former US Open finalist Greg Rusedski thinks he knows who is coming out of each group. Speaking on his podcast, ' Off Court with Greg ', Rusedski said: "Zverev is the favourite for the title.
 "He's the number one seed. He's won it twice. Alcaraz still hasn't won this event. Everybody's forgetting Turin is at altitude. What does that mean? The ball goes through the air quicker. So who does that help? Big servers.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "So for me, if I'm looking at the McEnroe group, I'm looking at Zverev and Shelton to come out of that group. The other thing which is fascinating about that is, guess who's showing up this week? Juan Carlos Ferrero, with Mr Ben Shelton and Bryan Shelton there. So I think Zverev and Shelton are out of the McEnroe group.
 "And if I'm looking at the Lendl group, you're thinking Alcaraz gets out of that if he's healthy and the stomach and the knee are fine. And then it's been between Medvedev and Tiafoe. No disrespect to Cobolli. He's not getting through that group. The court is too quick for him and low bouncing.
 "So I'm kind of edging towards Medvedev just because of the experience sneaking out of that one. But it's a little bit of a 50-50 with Medvedev and Tiafoe. But I'm thinking we're getting a Zverev-Alcaraz final. That's what is going to happen there.
 "Sascha has something to prove because we've been all talking, oh, he hasn't beaten Carlos. Oh, he hasn't beaten Sinner. So I'm going to go for Mr Zverev to get his mojo back and win his third end-of-season championship, even though on paper the favourite is Carlos Alcaraz."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Despite recording his best-ever season on the ATP Tour, Zverev has failed to beat either Carlos Alcaraz or Jannik Sinner in 2026. He lost to the Spaniard in their sole meeting at the Australian Open and has fallen to the Italian in each of their five clashes this year.
